theme.title: Across the NBA
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many seconds does an NBA team have to shoot under the shot clock?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The NBA has had a 24-second limit since 1954.

funFacts.text: Danny Biasone and Leo Ferris first tested the shot-clock idea at a Syracuse Nationals scrimmage.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Danny Biasone and general manager Leo Ferris experimented with a 24-second shot clock during a scrimmage

funFacts.text: Biasone arrived at the timing by counting shot attempts in basketball's most entertaining games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: I noticed each team took about 60 shots. That meant 120 shots per game.

funFacts.text: Before the rule, teams protecting a lead could stall endlessly by passing without shooting.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Teams in the lead were running out the clock, passing the ball incessantly

questions.prompt: How many games did San Antonio win in its unbeaten March of 2014?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: an unbeaten month in March (16–0)

funFacts.text: The late-season surge continued into the start of April.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a 19-game winning streak from late February to early April

funFacts.text: Dallas later stretched the Spurs to seven games in the playoff opener.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: defeated the Dallas Mavericks in seven games in the first round

funFacts.text: San Antonio returned to the Finals to face Miami in a rematch.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: back-to-back Finals appearances, also against the Miami Heat

questions.prompt: Dennis Rodman was drafted in the second round in 1986. What overall pick was he?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: as the third pick in the second round (27th overall)

funFacts.text: Rodman played at Southeastern Oklahoma State, far from the NCAA's traditional blueblood programs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Southeastern Oklahoma State

funFacts.text: His performance at the Portsmouth Invitational Tournament was what helped catch Detroit's eye.

source.quote: where he won Most Valuable Player honors and caught the attention of the Detroit Pistons

funFacts.text: He joined Chuck Daly's 'Bad Boys,' with Isiah Thomas and Joe Dumars leading the backcourt.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: joining the rugged team of coach Chuck Daly that was called "Bad Boys"

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Amar'e Stoudemire average in the 2005 playoffs?
questions.note: 29.9 points per game across Phoenix's playoff run.

funFacts.text: Stoudemire also averaged 10.7 rebounds during that postseason.
He scored 40 points in the opening game of Phoenix's series against Dallas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: May 9 Dallas W 127–102 Amar'e Stoudemire (40)

funFacts.text: Phoenix's postseason ended in the Western Conference Finals against the eventual champion San Antonio Spurs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Suns lost 4–1 to the 2-seed, and eventual NBA champion, San Antonio Spurs

questions.prompt: Jimmy Butler had 40 points and 11 rebounds in Game 3 of the 2020 Finals. How many assists did he add?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Butler finished with 40 points, 11 rebounds and 13 assists for a triple-double to lead Miami to a 115–104 win

funFacts.text: Miami won that game without starters Bam Adebayo and Goran Dragić, who were sidelined.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: as Heat starters Adebayo and Dragić remained sidelined

funFacts.text: Butler became the first player to outscore, outrebound and out-assist LeBron James in the same Finals game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Butler also became the first player to have more points, rebounds and assists in a Finals game than James

funFacts.text: Miami's starters outscored the Lakers' starters despite the Heat entering the game behind in the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Miami's starters outscored the Lakers' starters 89–51
